title: UAV-X run record
description: Provenance contract for runs/*.jsonl. Round 2 finding 5: nothing tied runs/latest.jsonl to the scenario that had just run, so a stale green file survived a crashed simulation and a metrics writer that never saw a vehicle could satisfy a gate. uavx_eval.check validates this block before reading any metric. A metric can only be trusted after its provenance is. Round 3 finding 6: packet counts and injected events were optional, and there was no duration, so a short run with no events could satisfy every requirement. They are required now. Round 6 finding 5: observations, handback and relay_slot were defined here and required by nothing, so the run that proves the communication mark could omit all three and still validate. They are required per scenario through the allOf block at the end, which is why jsonschema_mini now implements if and then.

run_id.description: Unique per run. The filename is runs/<run_id>.jsonl.

scenario_path.description: Repo-relative path of the scenario. The checker rejects a mismatch against what the gate asked for, which is what stops a previous scenario's record passing a later gate.

scenario_sha256.description: Hash of the scenario file as actually read, so an edited scenario cannot reuse an old result.

seed.description: RNG seed taken from the scenario. Same seed and same commit must reproduce the run exactly.

completion.description: Only 'complete' is accepted. latest.jsonl is published by atomic rename after every process exits cleanly, never by append.

vehicle_ids_observed.description: Must match the scenario's vehicle list. A run that saw two of four vehicles is not the run the gate asked for.

pose_sample_count.description: Zero means nothing was ever observed, which is how 'no samples' masquerades as 'no separation violations'.

app_packets_sent_by_node.description: Denominators. A zero denominator makes any ratio meaningless and is rejected rather than treated as 1.0.

delivered_hops_by_node.description: Mean hop count of DELIVERED APPLICATION packets only. HELLO and LSA traffic must not be counted; including it lets a swarm with no relaying show a hop count above 1.

injected_events.description: Every event the scenario asked for, with the time it was actually observed. An event that never fired fails the gate instead of leaving a default reconnect time in place.

versions.description: Every ENFORCED key from stage-1/setup/versions.lock, read at run time. Round 4 finding 8: this block named four of them, so a run could be labelled with an incomplete version object and attributed to a stack it did not come off. The ROS middleware version belongs here more than most: rmw_fastrtps carries every message this project measures. The observed_ keys in the lock are context for a human and are deliberately not required.

metrics.description: The numbers the gates assert on. Present only after every provenance field above has validated.

requested_duration_s.description: Duration the scenario asked for. Without it a 20 second run can send the minimum packet count and claim completion instead of running the frozen duration.

elapsed_sim_s.description: Simulated time actually elapsed. uavx_eval.check rejects a run shorter than 95% of requested_duration_s.

source_tree_sha256.description: Hash of the source that can change what a simulation does, from scripts/source_tree_hash.py: uavx_ws/, scenarios/, scripts/ and stage-1/setup/. Deliberately narrower than the repository, so editing a sentence of prose does not invalidate a week of runs, and deliberately wider than commit_sha, which ignores uncommitted code. W5 requires this to equal the source_tree_sha256 in submission/source-manifest.json, which is what ties the evidence to the code being submitted.

contact_monitor_samples.description: Zero contacts means nothing if no monitor was attached. The safety gate requires this above zero.

observations.description: Round 5 finding 5 asked what delivered-once means. Round 6 finding 5 is right that counts alone cannot answer it: a record saying generated 450 and unique_delivered 450 is satisfied by 450 deliveries of the wrong 450 packets. The two id sets go in, and the evaluator recomputes equality from them rather than trusting the arithmetic in the file. RFC 9171 makes the same separation, identity by source plus creation sequence on one side and delivery reports on the other.

generated_ids.description: origin_id:sequence for every observation the swarm produced during the run.

delivered_ids.description: origin_id:sequence for every observation the GCS accepted, deduplicated. Set equality with generated_ids is the claim.

duplicated.description: arrivals of an id the GCS already held. Not a failure; a number the record has to carry so unique_delivered cannot be inflated by retries.

peak_queue_depth.description: deepest any node's store-and-forward queue got, against the 512 packet size.

backlog_drain_s.description: route restored to backlog empty. Derived bound is 2.25 s: 450 packets at 200 per second.

control_queue_max_delay_s.description: worst time a HELLO, LSA or role message waited behind anything. Observations never delay control, so this stays small however deep the backlog got.

missing_ids.description: generated and never uniquely delivered. Empty is the claim, and it is what the evaluator prints when equality fails.

unexpected_ids.description: delivered but never generated. Empty is the claim.

handback.description: Round 5 finding 1: the claim is that the recovered path carried data BEFORE the relay moved, and without timestamps and a named path, break-before-make and make-before-break produce identical records. Round 6 finding 7: the transaction also needs an owner. The coordinator rule is a property of the disconnected component, and by the time the handback runs the component has merged, so ownership is carried from the election rather than recomputed. The owner is never the relay.

epoch_owner.description: the node that opened the epoch and carried it to release. Must not be the relay.

staying_member.description: the member whose route the owner evaluated. In link_loss, uav_4.

prepared_path.description: the non-relay path named in PREPARE_RELEASE. The relay must not appear in it.

prepared_path_computations.description: consecutive computations the prepared path won before PREPARE_RELEASE. Route hysteresis is 2, and a path that appears once as the radio comes back is not one to hand a vehicle back on.

confirmed_observation_id.description: the observation the GCS acknowledged over the prepared path. This one id is what turns make-before-break from an intention into a fact.

release_sender.description: who sent RELEASE. Must be epoch_owner; a release from anyone else is the stale-owner case the design forbids.

release_at.description: later than confirmed_at, which is the whole make-before-break claim.

relay_slot.description: Round 5 finding 4: the slot clearance rule was never exercised by an accepted scenario, so nothing proved a future implementation would call it. The commanded slot and the clearance it was checked against go in the record.
